To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the distinctiveness of local features varies greatly across the descriptor space, (2) it is possible to estimate the distinctiveness of all descriptors with a linear time complexity in the number of database images, (3) the distinctiveness estimation is compatible with spatially constrained retrieval and (4) the least distinctive features do not contribute to the retrieval accuracy, but can be removed without any loss.

(a) the distinctiveness of a descriptor is not a constant, but varies in a non-trivial manner across the descriptor space, and (b) the distinctiveness can be estimated efficiently and accurately, which leads to a new state of the art in visual place recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving large-scale visual place recognition, by adapting the Hamming Embedding approach to account for varying local descriptor distinctiveness.
improving large scale visual place recognition by accounting for the distinctiveness of local features.
developing scalable methods for improving large-scale place recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is the most efficient, scalable and accurate method for estimating local descriptor distinctiveness, and therefore the most suitable for visual place recognition in large-scale datasets.
DisLoc is a novel method which is simple, fast, and scalable to very large databases.
our proposed approach outperforms all competing baselines on the considered datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DisLoc is the first unsupervised method that can be applied to large scale databases, while outperforming all competing methods.
we present an efficient and effective way to estimate the distinctiveness of local descriptors.
we have developed a method that can efficiently estimate distinctiveness for all descriptors in a database, and that this distinctiveness can be used to improve retrieval accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
descriptor distinctiveness is a key factor in large scale visual place recognition and can be efficiently estimated using a simple, unsupervised method.
distinctiveness of local image features is an important factor in visual object retrieval.
the performance of a visual place recognition system can be improved by simply accounting for the distinctiveness of descriptors in the database, which can be estimated in a fully unsupervised way.
